answer.rationale: The two acute declines (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%) point at a funnel/time-to-value problem, and memory_86 plus memory_31 converge on onboarding/signup friction reduction as the lever that moves exactly those metrics. That is a more durable fix than matching the competitor's entry price, which is why I am spending verification on memory_86 (the load-bearing basis for my intended action) and memory_73 (the tempting alternative I most want to disconfirm before rejecting it). Two caveats I am holding rather than resolving: every inherited memory is a summary with no effect size, sample size, or durability window, so 'improved completion rates' may be a small or already-harvested lift, and memory_31 is the oldest record (day 12) — the field cuts it describes may already be shipped, meaning the remaining headroom is thin. Downstream value risk is real in both directions: promotional pricing (memory_73) reports 'strong acquisition and revenue lift' but says nothing about renewal quality or margin, so it may be buying discount-driven revenue that fails the sustainable-qualified-revenue objective; and onboarding simplification carries the mirror-image risk that stripping fields raises raw activation while degrading lead qualification and downstream pipeline quality — the same tension memory_44 hints at with sales-assisted enterprise flows. So I will run this as a standard experiment with qualified-revenue and lead-quality guardrails, not just a completion-rate readout, and I will not treat an activation lift alone as success. If verification shows memory_86's lift was marginal or already captured, activation_messaging (memory_91) is my fallback since it targets the larger of the two declines.
